liquid.survey: Stats NZ, Household Economic Survey, household net worth statistics, year ended June 2021

note: The World Inequality Database (WID.world, bulk download of 15 October 2026, read again in that of 30 October 2026), New Zealand, 2024: average net personal wealth (ahweal992j) and average post-tax national income (adiinc992j) per adult over 20, resources split equally within couples, in NZD of that year, for the bottom 20, 40, 60, 90 and 99 percent and the top 1 percent; each family's band is read from them. Read 2026-10-30. Savings (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-30: only what a family holds as deposits and cash): Stats NZ, Household net worth statistics: Year ended June 2021 (corrected workbook), Table 2.02 Household assets and liabilities, mean value, by net-worth quintile, year ended June 2021, in $000s (times 1000 here; rounded to the nearest thousand at source, so Quintile 1's deposits of 6 and net worth of -5 are coarse). "Currency and deposits" is the liquid item. The workbook was read with openpyxl and Table 2.02 saved as CSV; its first block is 2021. Quintile 1's net worth is negative (-$5,000), so its share of net wealth is negative. No top 1 percent. Read again 2026-11-03 from the bulk download of 30 October 2026 (its country files dated 30 October 2026): every row quoted here, its year and its currency label stood as before, and no later year was given. Until 2026-11-03 this note and its sources wrote the variable codes with their age and population parts swapped (ahwealj992 for ahweal992j and adiincj992 for adiinc992j), codes no file of the database holds (its README: type, concept, age group, population, as in sptinc992j), and called adiinc992j post-tax disposable income, which its metadata names post-tax national income ([Post-tax national income]=[Post-tax disposable income]+[Public spending]). Its other sources were fetched again on 2026-11-03 and said the same. The national accounts (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03: each band's income scaled by households' disposable income over national income), read 2026-11-03 from the OECD's sector accounts (DSD_NASEC10@DF_TABLE14), 2023: the net disposable income (B.6n) of households (S.14), 242,491 less 9,533 (232,958), and net national income (B.5n) 405,220 less 63,185 (342,035), in millions of the national currency, a ratio of about 0.681 (`cash`). Each net figure was derived as the gross less its own consumption of fixed capital (P.51c), from the same table, series and year. 2023 was the latest year published. Until 2026-11-03 each band's income was the database's post-tax national income as it stood, public spending included.
